column3: The FBI has fired four agents who worked on former Special Counsel Jack Smith's team investigating Trump, although some of those terminations were later reversed. The move is the latest in a string of personnel actions targeting employees who worked on probes looking into Trump or his allies.
Trump again threatens to withhold federal funds from New York City if Democratic candidate Mamdani wins the mayoral election

CBS news heavily edits "60-minutes* interview with Trump. The 90-minute interview was edited down to 28 mins. This is notable as Trump  he had sued CBS over the editing of a 60 Minutes interview with then-Vice President Kamala Harris, which he alleged had been deceptively edited to help her chances in the presidential election.
US citizen shot from behind as he warned ICE agents about children gathering at a bus stop
Three killed in another US military strike on alleged drug boat in the Caribbean. This is the 15th such strike since early September and brings the death toll to at least 64

There's no due process': ICU nurse, army veteran among U.S. citizens caught in ICE dragnet. ICE also leaned into criticisms - in one incident, agents were videotaped taunting Peace Patrol activists from their van saying, “Good morning ladies! A-kidnapping we will go.”
Trump threatens to go into Nigeria ‘guns-a-blazing’ over attacks on Christians. US president says he ordered Pentagon to begin planning for action, without mentioning Muslim persecution
President suggests being "anti-Trump" is ‘probably illegal’ in social media rant about Seth Meyers, where he called Meyers a "deranged lunatic", "100% Anti Trump" and asked why NBC employs him

400 people detained for hours at a privately owned race track about an hour west of Boise as part an FBI-led investigation into illegal gambling that resulted in more than 100 arrests, nearly all for immigration violations. Five families interviewed by The Associated Press said officers zip-tied children as young as 11. They said an 8-year-old boy got glass in his mouth as he screamed while officers broke his car window.  The operation is a striking example of how immigration has become a major driver across federal law enforcement

Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth has ordered the military to provide dozens of lawyers to the Justice Department for temporary assignments. The assignments are in Memphis and near the U.S.-Mexico border. The Trump administration increasingly has tapped the military to bolster its immigration crackdown

North Carolina Republican spokesman urged reporter from ProPublica to drop news story on a prominent conservative state Supreme Court judge, with a veiled threat. He said "I’m sure you’re aware of our connections with the Trump Administration and I’m sure they would be interested in this matter,”. He later posted on social media that Trump should “feed ProPublica to the USAID wood chipper.”

Miami Herald reports that the Trump Administration has made the decision to attack military installations inside Venezuela and the strikes could come at any moment. There has been no Congressional approval for action. [Note that the White House denies this report]

Republican chairman and senior Democrat on the Armed Services Committee said that the Pentagon had not handed over information about the boat attacks in the Caribbean and Pacific despite repeated requests.
ICE agents clash with Chicago-area residents over Halloween, chasing suspects through front yards, driving SUVs onto sidewalks and using chemical agents during confrontations with furious residents

No high-level US representative to attend UN's COP30 climate talks. The US has always sent delegations of various sizes to UN climate summits over the past three decades, even during periods under George W Bush and in Donald Trump’s first term. This decision underscores administration’s hostility to climate action

Dept of Justice (DoJ)asked election officials in Fulton county, Georgia, to turn over records related to the 2020 election. This underscores how the administration is trying to revive one of Trump's biggest falsehoods about the 2020 election
Virginia (Democrat) and Ohio (Republican) advance redistricting plans to skew congressional seats in Democrat and Republican favour, respectively

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) quietly formalized sweeping changes to a federal immigration database Friday, turning it into a national “voter verification” tool that appears to sidestep federal privacy protections and will make it easier to remove large numbers of voters from the rolls.

A new White House rule issued Friday restricts the ability of credentialed journalists to freely access the offices of press secretary Karoline Leavitt and other top communications officials in the West Wing, near the Oval Office. The White House Correspondents’ Association, which represents journalists covering the White House, said the new restrictions would hinder reporters' ability to question officials, ensure transparency and hold government accountable

Trump’s war on ‘woke’ forces community lenders to cut services or close. The Trump administration has withheld $324 million in funding appropriated by Congress for the nearly 1,400 CDFIs (community lenders) across the country, targeting them as part of a "woke" program, that promotes a “partisan agenda,” “gender extremism” and “climate radicalism." At the beginning of the government shutdown,Russell Vought issued reduction-in-service notices to all staffers of the CDFI Fund, the agency that provides grants and certifies CDFIs, indicating their employment would be terminated on December 13
Defense Scretary Hegseth said the Pentagon is moving "quickly" on Trump’s directive to restart nuclear weapons testing to ensure the U.S. has the “most capable” nuclear arsenal in the world.

Trump calling for filibuster rule to be scrapped so the Republican majority can bypass Democrats and reopen government. The filibuster is the Senate rule for agreement by 60 of its 100 members to pass most legislation. Trump wrote on Social Media: "It is now time for the Republicans to play their "TRUMP CARD," and go for what is called the Nuclear Option — Get rid of the Filibuster, and get rid of it, NOW,"

Kristi Noem says in a press conference that “No American citizens have been arrested or detained” by immigration agents. This is false, with many verified instances of American citizens being arrested and detained

Access to gender-affirming care for transgender youth will be dramatically restricted by the Trump administration under new proposals by the Department of Health and Human Services. Both supporters and opponents of transgender rights agree that, if implemented, the proposals could make access to pediatric gender-affirming care across the country extremely difficult, if not impossible

Most of the government editorial staff at "Preventing Chronic Disease", an academic journal published by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) for more than 2 decades, have been told they’re being terminated, leaving the publication’s future uncertain.

The senior head of a Navy office that helps organize critical research and funding for the service has been replaced by a 33-year-old former Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) employee . His replacement is highly unusual given that the office — created by Congress in 1946 to fund Navy and Marine Corps research — is typically run by a two-star admiral with extensive experience in technology, science, and engineering.

Trump's administration has launched a website to recruit more law enforcement officers to police Washington DC., as it seeks to expand its control over the nation's capital. The website advertises openings at Immigration and Customs Enforcement, the Drug Enforcement Administration and the U.S. Park Police. Hires will be stationed in Washington DC, for up to one year, according to the website

The Trump administration is going to restrict the number of refugees it admits into the United States next year to the token level of just 7,500 – and those spots will mostly be filled by white South Africans. The low number represents a dramatic drop after the US previously allowed in hundreds of thousands of people fleeing war and persecution from around the world.
Democratic lawmakers excluded from briefing on US military strikes in South America
After Democrat Senator Chuck Schumer criticised the outcome of Trump's trip to Asia, Trump retaliates and suggests that criticism of him is ‘almost treasonous’

US immigration officials have been increasingly detaining people in small, secretive holding facilities for days or even weeks at a time in violation of federal policy. These holding facilities are often small concrete rooms with no beds and are designed to only be used for a few hours

A progressive Democratic candidate for the House of Representatives and several other Chicago officials are facing federal charges stemming from protests outside an ICE facility. She faces one count of conspiracy and one charge alleging that she “forcibly impeded, intimidated and interfered” with an officer. Videos of her interactions with officers at the scene — including incidents where she is shoved to the ground and beaten in the face with a baton — have been shared widely across social media
Dept of Homeland Security (DHS) showing old and misleading video footage of protests to push its deportation narrative and to justify federal law enforcement in Democrat-run cities
Defense Secretary Hegseth extends DC National Guard deployment until February 2026 (the deployment was set to expire at the end of November)

Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem saying that ICE will be out in "full force" in Chicago over Halloween. Noem rejected a request from Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker (D) to pause Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) operations on the holiday to let children trick or treat without fearing a confrontation with armed federal agents

Pentagon orders states’ national guards to form ‘quick reaction forces’ for ‘crowd control’. A memo signed by the director of operations for the Pentagon’s national guard bureau details plan to train over 20,000 national guard members across the US to carry out Trump’s order on subduing civil unrest
Trump directs Pentagon to match Russia and China in nuclear weapons testing
Dept of Justice (DOJ) suspends two prosecutors who said 'mob' of 'rioters' carried out Jan. 6 attack on the capitol in 2021

Utah plans to place as many as 1,300 homeless people in what supporters call a services campus and critics deem a detention camp. Although plans existed before they have been accelerated after Trump issued an executive order in July

Radio Free Asia, one of four federally funded news organizations the Trump administration has aimed to close, will shut down its news operations at the end of October. The news group’s expected closure can be attributed to the Trump administration’s broad efforts to cut federal funding, and to the government shutdown

Donald Trump has fired all six members of an independent federal agency responsible for reviewing his controversial White House ballroom and planned “Arc de Trump” in Washington DC. The White House says it will appoint new Commission of Fine Arts members ‘more aligned with … America First Policies’

The Trump administration took another step Tuesday to weaken protections for Americans with medical debt, issuing new guidance that threatens ongoing state efforts to keep that debt off consumers’ credit reports. Many States have passed laws to protect consumer credit but The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau now asserts that federal law bars states from restricting medical debts from credit reports.
Man deported to Laos despite US court order blocking his removal. District judge told ICE to keep Alabama man in US while he showed what judge called ‘substantial claim’ to citizenship
Health Secretary RFK Jr asks Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) to study alleged harms of offshore wind farms
House Republicans revive Biden "auto-pen' claims. Although they offer no evidence in their report, they urge Attorney General Pam Bondi to launch a full investigation

Federal judge censured top Trump administration officials for making several out-of-court statements against Kilmar Abrego Garcia. U.S. District Judge Waverly Crenshaw said many prejudicial comments from Attorney General Pam Bondi, Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem and other senior officials violated a local court rule and threatened Abrego Garcia’s right to a fair trial

Nigerian Nobel laureate Wole Soyinka says US revoked his non-immigrant visa.The 91-year-old writer said in 2016 that he had torn up his U.S. green card and renounced his American residency in protest at the first election of President Donald Trump.
Trump tells American troops in Japan that he is prepared to send "more than the National Guard" into American Cities

The U.S. president’s family raked in more than $800 million from sales of crypto assets in the first half of 2025 alone, a Reuters examination found, on top of potentially billions more in unrealized “on paper” gains. Much of that cash has come from foreign sources as Donald Trump's sons have touted their business on an international investor roadshow.

U.S. military officials involved with President Donald Trump's expanding operations in Latin America have been asked to sign non-disclosure agreements, three U.S. officials say. The step is highly unusual, given that U.S. military officials are already required to shield national security secrets from public view, and comes as lawmakers in Congress say they are being kept in the dark about key aspects of the mission
US military kills 14 in new attacks on vessels in the Pacific, according to Hegseth. Justification for the strikes has been widely disputed by legal experts

Texas Attorney Tim Paxton sues Tylenol makers, accusing them of knowingly hiding the drug's links to autism and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder. There is no good evidence that tylenol (paracetamol) is linked to autism or ADHD

Trump administration planning to revamp ICE leadership by reassigning multiple directors of field offices and replacing them with border patrol agents, as it seeks to intensify its mass deportation efforts.

Trump attacks Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell again, calling him incompetent: "We have an incompetent head of the Fed... we got a bad Fed guy, but he'll be out of there in a few months, and we'll get somebody new,"

Trump administration alters White House website to include alleged Democrat scandals. The web page includes a “Major Events Timeline,” which details the renovations following the War of 1812 and the construction of the Oval Office in 1909, for example. But last week, the administration added a number of entries to the timeline about supposed misdeeds by the Clinton, Obama and Biden administrations — some of which included flagrant misinformation.

Trump demands "no early voting", threatening upcoming elections in New York and California and challenging legitimacy of ballots that are not cast in person on election day . Removing early voting will reduce the ability of citizens to participate in elections

ICE uses 'Halo' images to dehumanize immigrants. One image included the phrase "Destroy the Flood," alongside a link to an ICE recruitment page. DHS appears to be equating the Flood, the main antagonists of the Halo series, with immigrants. For context, the Flood are a parasitic alien species that infect and consume sentient life across the galaxy.

Justice Dept (DoJ) asks Supreme Court (SCOTUS) to allow firing of the head of the Copyright Office. Trump had fired Shira Perlmutter following a report on AI and copyright legality in May, but a lower court temporarily reinstated her.
Trump rules out running for vice president in the 2028 election but declined to definitively say he would not seek a third term

Threat to US vaccines as entire staff supporting Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) were let go as well as its Ethics and CDC's Human Resources department. This is according to former Chief Medical Officer Debra Houry and Demetre Daskalakis, former director of the National Center for Immunization and Respiratory Diseases who spoke at. a press conference
CNN boss told staff to ease bck on White House demolition reporting after a visit to the White House last week. CNN denies the report.
Trump demands a ban on ‘fake ads’ that show off his shrinking polling numbers on his social media platform, Truth Social

US transportation secretary, Sean Duffy, says he’ll revoke $160m from California over non-citizen truck licenses. Duffy says state is illegally issuing commercial driver’s licenses, but California DMV spokesperson says California is complying with law
Republican Indiana governor calls special session to redraw congressional maps. GOP-led state is latest that Trump administration has put pressure on to undertake redistricting to favor Republicans

Trump on social media gives new warning on pregnant women taking Tylenol (Paracetamol), or giving Tylenol to their children. He also said parents should split vaccination visits for many childhood vaccines. There is no evidence for harm for Tylenol or combine vaccines. More visits will reduce uptake, and for some diseases the combined vaccines are more effective than single shots.
USS Gravely, a guided missile destroyer, docks in Trinidad and Tobago, increasing military pressure on neighbouring Venezuela

US detains British Muslim journalist, Sami Hamdi, during speaking tour, revoked his visa and said he would be deported. Hamdi has been critical of Israel's actions in Gaza and Conservative activist Laura Loomer on Sunday took credit for Hamdi’s arrest.

The Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) website has placed an advisory blaming Senate Democrats for the impending absence of food assistance benefits (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP)) on its website. This violates the Hatch Act.

Trump administration is rejecting the idea of using roughly $5 billion in contingency funds to keep food aid flowing into November amid the government shutdown, according to a Department of Agriculture memo.

A key Trump ally, conservative attorney Mike Davis, says a federal grand jury has been empaneled in Florida that will begin meeting in January to investigate what he calls a decade-long conspiracy against Donald Trump, with potential criminal charges against top Democratic figures. Davis is a close friend and informal adviser to Attorney General Pam Bondi

President Trump doubled down on Saturday in his feud with Canada over a television ad that used audio of former President Ronald Reagan denouncing tariffs, saying he would punish the country with an additional 10 percent tariff on its goods

Timothy Mellon, reclusive billionaire, anti-tax crusader and a major financial backer of Donald Trump has been named by anonymous sources as the private donor who gave $130m to the government to help pay US troops during the federal shutdown
“I’m the speaker and the president,” Mr. Trump has joked, according to two people who heard the remark, emphasising his control over Congressional Republicans.

Deputy White House Chief of Staff for Policy Stephen Miller told Fox host Will Cain that anyone attempting to interfere with ICE operations could be arrested for engaging in a “criminal conspiracy” against the United States, including Illinois Governor JB Pritzker.
Health secretary RFK Jr (Kennedy) to urge American to eat more saturated fats, contradicting decades of dietary guidelines

U.S. Border Patrol Commander Gregory Bovino was recorded throwing what appeared to be a tear gas canister at protesters in Chicago. violating a temporary restraining order that bans the use of tear gas, pepper spray and other tactics against journalists and protesters unless under imminent threat. DHS claims he has struck in the head by a rock thrown by a protester, however witnesses challenegd this.
Steve Bannon, former Trump ally and right-wing media executive, states "there is a plan" for Trump to be president in 2028 for a third term

Financial Times reports that "dozens of [interviewed] figures, including lawmakers, private sector executives, retired senior military figures and intelligence chiefs, current and former Trump officials, Washington lawyers and foreign government officials. Such is the fear of jail, bankruptcy or professional reprisal, that most of these people insisted on anonymity. This was in spite of the fact that many of the same people also wanted to emphasise that Trump would only be restrained by powerful voices opposing him publicly."

Federal immigration agents blanketed Chicago‘s affluent areas, making immigration arrests in previously less-targeted neighborhoods. Agents smashed one man‘s car window outside a family health center where his pregnant partner had an appointment. Other agents grabbed two construction workers from a house and teargassed neighbors on the residential block

Trump’s Son Is Poised to Profit From Pentagon Drone Proposal. A small company that has been manufacturing motors domestically for only a few weeks and has Donald Trump Jr. as an adviser won a parts order from the Army

Treasury Department imposes sanctions on Colombian president Petro, Interior Minister Armando Benedetti, as well as Petro's wife and eldest son. All are barred from accessing assets and any properties they may have in the US.

Trump suggested that former Special Counsel Jack Smith, former Attorney General Merrick Garland and other Biden administration officials “should be prosecuted” over their involvement in the investigation into the president’s alleged efforts to overturn the 2020 election results. He also named former FBI Director Christopher Wray and former Deputy Attorney General Lisa Monaco.

Pentagon accepts $130 million from private donor to help pay troops during government shutdown (this would equate to $100 per service member). The move to pay the troops with private donations is highly unusual and a potential violation of the Antideficiency Act, which prohibits federal agencies from spending money in excess of congressional appropriations or from accepting voluntary services.
Trump reverses Biden-era rule on copper smelters - the rule had imposed stricter limits on emissions.

Pentagon deploys top aircraft carrier USS Gerald Ford to the Caribbean. The carrier holds dozens of fighter jets and is also accompanied by several other smaller warships. This is a major escalation in the administration’s war against drug cartels, providing the resources to start conducting strikes against targets on the ground
Justice Deptartment (DoJ) seeks to deport Kilmar Abrego Garcia to Liberia

The United States has carried out another military strike against what it claimed was a vessel carrying illegal drugs in the Caribbean, killing six people onboard, the Pentagon chief, Pete Hegseth, said. Legal experts have suggested that simply characterizing gangs and drug cartels as terrorist organizations did not give the administration any additional authority to use lethal force

Donald Trump has announced an immediate end to all trade negotiations with Canada over an advert critical of the tariffs he has imposed on the nation. The advert, sponsored by the government of Canada's province of Ontario, quoted Trump's predecessor, Ronald Reagan, an icon of US conservatism, saying tariffs "hurt every American".

Trump administration announced a plan to allow oil and gas drilling in Alaska’s Arctic National Wildlife Refuge, one of the largest remaining tracts of pristine wilderness in the United States. In addition the Interior Department said it would hold an oil and gas lease sale in the coastal plain as soon as this winter.

Traditional enforcement by federal regulatory agencies has dropped dramatically since the Trump administration took office in January. In the first half of 2025, federal agency enforcement actions in the areas of consumer protection, competition, and financial practices were down 37% compared to the first half of 2024

Trump gives disaster relief to Republican states, but denies Maryland, Vermont and Illinois (all Democrat). Trump touted on social media that he had “won BIG” in Alaska in the last three presidential elections and that it was his “honor” to deliver for the “incredible Patriots” of Missouri, a state he also won three times.

Trump says he won't ask for declaration of war from Congress against South American cartels but "we're just gonna kill people that are bringing drugs into our country. We're going to kill them. They're going to be, like dead."

Pentagon announces "new generation" press corps - numerous right-wing, pro-Trump online outlets said they were among those that had agreed to the rules.This follows new rules by the Pentagon demanding approval on all stories, with many mainstream news outlets refusing to sign a new agreement and thus losing access

Lindesy Halligan interim prosecutor in the James Comey case, auto-deleted Signal messages exchanged with a law journalist, raising concerns that she is violating the Federal Records Act and the Justice Departments own record retention policy

Trump pardons founder of Binance, world’s largest crypto exchange. Changpeng Zhao pleaded guilty to failing to stop money laundering in 2023 (including by terrorist organisations) and was sentenced to four months. Trump’s pardon is another sign of the administration’s shift toward easing scrutiny on the crypto industry, at a time when Trump and his family are building their own multibillion dollar crypto empire and entered into a joint venture with Binance in May 2025.

Dept of Homeland Security (DHS) spokesperson confirms that Customs and Border Protection (CBP) border patrol agents, Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) deportation officers, Secret Service special agents, and Transportation Security Administration air marshals  will be receiving "superchecks" including lost pay and overtime, while over 700,000 federal workers are not receiving pay during the government shutdown.

Trump’s ‘election integrity’ chief claimed president has future powers to declare voting emergency. Heather Honey’s statements follow president’s aggressive effort to radically reshape elections before 2026
ICE has recruited some people into its training program without full vetting. The recruits have had criminal backgrounds or failed drug tests or were unable to meet physical or academic standards,
US strikes another boat alllegedly carrying drugs in the Pacific, raising the overall number of attacks to 9 and the death toll to 37.

The University of Virginia has reached a deal with adminstration to end investigations against it and restore funding. It agreed to be bound by federal guidance forbidding racial discrimination in admission and hiring, as described by the Justice Department. It also agreed to provide relevant data on a quarterly basis through 2028. The president will have to personally certify that the university is in compliance each quarter

A flurry of conservative commentators and US Senator Ted Cruz accused Democrats of passing off old footage from a 2017 rally as the crowd that attended a "No Kings" protest in opposition to President Donald Trump, with some claiming MSNBC was in on the alleged deception. But the video aired by MSNBC was, in fact, current; it authentically depicted the throngs of people who swarmed Boston Common for an October 18, 2025 demonstration.
Trump demolishes the entire historic White House East Wing to make room for new ballroom. Trump initially said the construction would not touch the East Wing or “interfere with the current building.”
Pregnant women report medical neglect in ICE detention, including miscarriages, delayed care, being shackled, as well as held in solitary confinement

Trump administration considering curbs on exports to China made with US software. Plan would include everything from laptops to jet engines, to retaliate against Beijing’s latest round of rare earth export restrictions
US demands EU reverse its climate and human rights rules in order to allow greater imports of liquefied natural gas (LNG)
Trump officials refer Biden-era Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) staff to Dept of Justice (DoJ) for potential criminal charges, alleging politicization of emergency funding.
North Carolina lawmakers give final approval to new congressional map that could give Republicans one more seat in the US House
U.S. Expands Antidrug Campaign With Strike on Boat in Pacific Near Colombia. It was the eighth known strike, and the first outside of the Caribbean,

Further to his previous demand, Donald Trump declared himself the arbiter of whether or not his own administration should pay him damages over past federal investigations. The president insisted on Tuesday that the government owes him “a lot of money” for previous justice department investigations into his conduct, while at the same time asserting his personal authority over any potential payout.

Committee on the Judiciary Chairman, Jim Jordan (Republican, Ohio),  referred former Director of the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) John Brennan to the Department of Justice for criminal prosecution over ‘Russiagate,’. He is latest the latest Trump foe in DOJ crosshairs

Trump fires another Inspector General. With the firing of Parisa Salehi, the Export-Import Bank’s inspector general, the president has now sidelined around two dozen of the watchdogs who seek out fraud and mismanagement in federal agencies

Trump tells Democrats he won't meet with them until government reopens, referenicng a request from U.S. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries to meet "anytime, anyplace." This breaks with past practice, as presidents have typically continued talks with congressional leaders during shutdowns, to try to reach a resolution

ICE raid targets vendors of counterfeit goods in Manhattan. Military-style trucks drove through Lower Manhattan escorted by armed federal agents. Military helicopters flew over the scene. The NYPD said they had no involvement and this was an ICE enforcement operation. According to the Dept of Homeland Security (DHS) this was a multi agency operation and involved agents from ICE, the FBI and the ATF

ICE (Immigration and Customs Enforcement) has spent more than $70 million on new weapons in the first nine months of President Donald Trump’s second term, a 700 percent increase on the same period in 2024, according to a report.
UN experts say US strikes against Venezuela in international waters amount to 'extrajudicial executions'

More than 420 anti-science bills attacking longstanding public health protections – vaccines, milk safety and fluoride – have been introduced in statehouses across the U.S. this year, part of an organized, politically savvy campaign to enshrine a conspiracy theory-driven agenda into law. the wave of legislation has cropped up in most states, pushed by people with close ties to Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.

U.S. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth has told Pentagon staff they must obtain permission before interacting with members of Congress, according to a congressional aide and a department memo. It is the latest example of the department working to control the flow of information about the world's most powerful military.
Fox News host Laura Ingraham joins business venture with Donald Trump Jr. Host often criticized Hunter Biden’s business on her show and said he capitalized on his father’s presidency for deals
North Carolina Republicans advance map to secure another seat in Congress. State house set to pass map to turn 10-4 Republican split into 11-3 – and state law does not give governor a veto

President Trump is demanding that the Justice Department pay him about $230 million in compensation for the federal investigations into him. The situation has no parallel in American history and is an example of potential ethical conflicts created by installing the president’s former lawyers atop the Justice Department

A group of dozens of officials from across the federal government, including U.S. intelligence officers, has been helping to steer President Donald Trump's drive for retribution against his perceived enemies, according to government records and a source familiar with the effort.

A divided U.S. appeals court ruled on Monday that Donald Trump can send National Guard troops into Portland, Oregon, despite objections by the leaders of the city and state. The unsigned majority opinion was joined by Circuit Judge Bridget Bade and Circuit Judge Ryan Nelson, who were both appointed by Trump in his first term. Circuit Judge Susan Graber, an appointee of Democratic President Bill Clinton, dissented. She said allowing troops to be called in response to "merely inconvenient" protests was "not merely absurd" but dangerous

Justice Department (DoJ) scrutinises Fani Willis over a trip to the Bahamas. President Trump had said that Ms. Willis, the prosecutor who brought election interference charges against him two years ago in Georgia, “should be prosecuted.”
Trump claims ‘unquestioned power’ in vow to send troops to San Francisco

Donald Trump urged Volodymyr Zelenskyy to accept Russia’s terms for ending its war in a volatile White House meeting, warning that Vladimir Putin had said he would “destroy” Ukraine if it did not agree. The meeting between the US and Ukrainian presidents descended many times into a “shouting match”, with Trump “cursing all the time”
US military strikes a seventh boat according to Defence Secretary Hegseth, killing three Colombians

Trump lashes out at Colombian president threatenting cuts to aid following the Colombian president accusing the US of killing an innocent Colombian fisherman in international waters in one of its strikes on boats in international waters
In response to mass "No Kings" protest, Trump posted AI-generated video of himself wearing a crown in a fighter jet dumping s*$t on protesters
The National Republican Senatorial Committee (NRSC) shares AI-generated video of Chuck Schumer praising the shutdown, to slam Democrats.

White House and other government agencies join Social Media platform Bluesky and use it to attack Democrats and blame them for the government shutdown. The administration has repeatedly thrust normally nonpartisan agencies into the funding fight, including by posting politically loaded language on agency websites
US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) tells airlines to disregard "X" sex markers and input "F'" or "M"

The US Senate is poised to approve Donald Trump’s nomination of an industry lobbyist to lead the Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) chemical safety office. If confirmed, the top four toxics office positions at the EPA will be held by former chemical industry lobbyists, raising new fears about the health and safety of the American public

US President Donald Trump has commuted the sentence of George Santos, a former Republican congressman serving seven years in prison for fraud and identify theft. Trump said Santos "has been horribly mistreated". Santos had admitted to stealing the identities of 11 people - including from his own family members
House speaker, Mike Johnson, refuses to swear in newly elected Democratic Congresswoman Grijalva, despite Democrats' legal threat. She was elected in a special election more than three weeks ago

Texas Governor Greg Abbott states he will deploy National Guard during "no kings" protest saying “Today, I directed the Dept of Public Safety and National Guard to surge forces into Austin ahead of an Antifa-linked protest"

Justice Department (DoJ) lawyers asked Supreme court to allow National Guard deployment in Chicago, setting up a high-stakes test for SCOTUS, to see if justices are going to agree with Trumps efforts to deploy states-based troops to US cities
Republican lawmakers ask Dept of Justice (DoJ) to investigate former special counsel Jack Smith. This comes a day or two after Trump publicly called for Smith's prosecution
ICE arrests Chicago area cop legally working in the US, who had passed FBI background check and had valid work authorisation
Pentagon criticises Netflix for making "woke garbage" after airing gay military drama "Boots" [attacking culture/the arts]
Prosecutor and her deputy who rejected Trump's pressure to charge New York state attorney general Letitia James are fired by Dept of Justice (DoJ)

Trump administration freezes another $11 billion for infrastructure projects in democratic states,. Russell Vought, the head stated on social media that the US army corps of engineers would pause work on “low priority” projects in cities such as New York, San Francisco, Boston and Baltimore. He said the projects could eventually be cancelled

The US military is holding two survivors on a Navy ship after the US carried out a Thursday strike on an alleged drug boat in the Caribbean, according to three US officials. It is unclear what the US is going to do with the survivors being detained, the sources said.
US blocks a global fee on shipping emissions as international meeting ends without new regulations
Trump files amended $15bn defamation complaint against New York Times. Refiled complaint, after judge tossed initial suit last month, also targets individual reporters and book publisher
Press secretary Karoline Leavitt states that ""The Democrat Party's main constituency is made up of Hamas terrorists, illegal aliens, and violent criminals."
Trump team preparing to install ‘allies’ at the IRS to target ‘major Democratic donors’ including George Soros
ProPrublica finds that more than 170 US Citizens have been held by immigration agents. They've been "kicked, dragged, and detained for days"
10,000 US forces are now supporting counter-narcotics efforts in the Caribbean, with a majority based in Puerto Rico. There are 8 Navy ships and one submarine in Caribbean waters
Trump plans to switch terrorism prevention funding from Democratic to Republican states. Overhaul of $1bn post-9/11 program would shift funds to states that voted for Trump in 2024 election
Queer and trans immigrants allege forced labor and sexual assault in ICE facility

The justice department filed federal charges against John Bolton, the former national security adviser to Donald Trump who turned into one of his biggest critics, accusing him of transmitting and retaining highly classified information. The indictment marked the third time in recent weeks the justice department has secured criminal charges against one of Trump’s critics.

JD Vance dismisses leaked racist text messages from Young Republicans as “stupid” jokes made by “kids.” - messages included references to gas chambers, Hitler, racism, gay slurs and rape. 8 of the 11 members of the group spanned ages 24-35, and hold positions in Republican politics
